status_changes.description: PASS must be sent after USER command for authentication
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites specific session observations (Sessions 1-8, 10) showing USER followed by 331, then PASS. This is direct observational evidence from traces.

status_changes.description: Data transfer commands (LIST, RETR, STOR, NLST) require successful authentication (USER/PASS completed)
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites that all data transfers in traces occur after successful PASS (230 response), with specific mention of Session 6 failure case. This is direct observational evidence.

status_changes.description: PASV or PORT should be sent before data transfer commands to establish data connection
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 4 observing PASV before LIST/STOR. While it notes other sessions may use active mode, the claim is supported by observed behavior in at least one trace.

status_changes.description: QUIT can be sent from any state to terminate session
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 9 where QUIT was sent immediately after connection (RESP_220), and states all sessions end with QUIT. This supports the claim that it can be sent from early states.

status_changes.description: After authentication failure (530), user may retry with USER command
status_changes.rationale: Evidence explicitly cites Session 2 and Session 6 where PASS failed with 530 and was followed by USER -> 331, PASS -> 230. Direct trace evidence.

status_changes.description: RNTO must follow RNFR command for rename operations
status_changes.rationale: Evidence relies on 'standard FTP requires' statement and count of occurrences (3 times each), but does not explicitly cite a trace sequence showing RNFR immediately preceding RNTO in a specific session. It is likely true but the evidence provided is partially documentary/heuristic.

status_changes.description: Initial server greeting (220) is received before any client commands
status_changes.rationale: Evidence states 'All sessions start with RESP_220 -> 220 before any client command'. This is a strong universal claim backed by observation of all sessions.

status_changes.description: TYPE command should be sent before data transfer if non-default transfer type needed
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 3 and Session 7 where TYPE was sent before RETR/STOR. Supports the conditional claim.

status_changes.description: FEAT command is typically sent after authentication to discover server capabilities
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 5 where FEAT was sent after PASS -> 230. Supports the 'typically' claim with an example.

status_changes.description: SYST command is typically sent after authentication
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 3 where SYST was sent after PASS -> 230. Supports the 'typically' claim with an example.

status_changes.description: CWD and PWD commands require successful authentication
status_changes.rationale: Evidence states 'All CWD and PWD commands in traces occur after successful PASS (230)'. Direct observational evidence.

status_changes.description: NOOP can be sent at any time during authenticated session as keepalive
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 10 where NOOP was sent between PASS and PWD. Demonstrates validity during authenticated session.
